evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/voice_commands.rs:531-556 - action_contact_manager is a LIVE voice-assistant webhook handler (dispatched from process_command via voice_intent::CONTACT_MANAGER at :172) that returns hardcoded PLACEHOLDER email addresses to residents: :537 'spravca@example.com' (sk), :538 'spravce@example.com' (cs), :539 'manager@example.com' (en). The same placeholder is echoed into the response card content (:549 content: "manager@example.com") and into the structured data payload (:554 "manager_email": "manager@example.com").

example.com is the IETF-reserved documentation domain (RFC 2606) and can never receive mail. A resident who asks the voice assistant to contact the manager is told, spoken aloud (the string is also wrapped into SSML at :546) and shown on-card, to email a non-functional address - i.e. the feature actively hands out wrong contact information rather than resolving the real property-manager / organization contact from the device's organization_id (available on the VoiceAssistantDevice: device.organization_id is used elsewhere in this file, e.g. action_check_announcements :409).

This is INCONSISTENT with the rest of this file, which was explicitly hardened against exactly this class of 'fabricated response on a live webhook' bug: action_check_balance (:262-268), action_check_announcements (:400-411) and action_check_meter (:472-495) all carry code-review comments ('code review: fabricated success/empty success') documenting a prior fix where a made-up answer was replaced by a real repository query. action_contact_manager was left with a hardcoded fake address and never wired to a contacts/organization lookup.

Fix (landable in isolation): resolve the manager/organization contact via a repository lookup keyed on device.organization_id (or device.unit_id -> building -> manager), and fall back to an honest 'contact details are not available via voice; please use the app' message (mirroring action_check_balance's fail-honestly branch) rather than emitting a reserved-domain placeholder. Confidence medium: the placeholder is statically certain and on a reachable production path; the user-facing impact severity (misdirected contact) is clear but not runtime-confirmed against a live skill, hence medium not high.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler/mod.rs:262-288 - Scheduler::start() spawns a SINGLE tokio task whose body is `loop { ticker.tick().await; self.run_scheduled_tasks().await; }`. run_scheduled_tasks (:290-405) sequentially awaits ~20 scheduled jobs (publish_scheduled_announcements, dispatch_announcement_notifications, activate_scheduled_votes, close_expired_votes, cleanup_sessions, expire_signature_requests, send_meter_reminders, send_payment_reminders, transition_overdue_invoices, fire_due_report_schedules, retention prunes, ...). Each job's Result::Err is caught and logged (if let Err(e) = ...), but a PANIC inside any awaited job (e.g. a slice/index panic, an unwrap in a called repository, an arithmetic overflow in debug) is NOT caught - there is no catch_unwind and no per-job tokio::spawn isolation - so it unwinds the whole loop task and the loop exits permanently.

backend/servers/api-server/src/main.rs:692 - the JoinHandle is bound to `let _scheduler_handle = scheduler.start();` and never awaited, polled, or supervised. Nothing calls .is_finished() or restarts the task, so if the loop panics ALL scheduled background work (announcement publishing, vote lifecycle transitions, invoice overdue transitions, payment/meter/signature reminders, session cleanup, data-retention prunes) silently stops for the entire process lifetime with no alert - a single transient panic degrades the system until an operator notices and restarts.

The SAME unsupervised pattern applies to the sibling background workers started immediately after: main.rs:704 `let _push_fanout_handle = push_fanout_worker.start();`, :715 `let _quiet_hours_drain_handle = quiet_hours_drain_worker.start();`, :727 `let _notification_digest_handle = notification_digest_worker.start();`. All four spawn-and-forget with a `_`-prefixed handle and no restart-on-exit supervision.

Fix (landable in isolation): wrap each scheduled job invocation so a panic is contained to that tick (e.g. run each job inside its own tokio::spawn and log JoinError on panic, or AssertUnwindSafe + .catch_unwind() around run_scheduled_tasks), AND/OR supervise the top-level worker handles (a small supervisor task that awaits each JoinHandle and re-spawns on unexpected exit, incrementing a metric). Confidence medium: the missing panic isolation and unsupervised handle are statically certain; whether a panic is actually reachable inside a specific job depends on downstream repository code outside this segment, so exploitability is not runtime-confirmed - but the blast radius (all background jobs stop) makes this a substantive resilience gap.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/voice_commands.rs:447-466 - action_book_facility returns VoiceActionResult { success: true, ... } (:459) while its response_text (:451-455) tells the user 'Facility booking is not yet available via voice assistant. Please use the mobile app or web portal.' The handler reports SUCCESS for a feature it explicitly did not perform.

This success flag is persisted and used for analytics, not just returned to the caller: process_command (:212-231) derives `success` from result and writes it into the voice_command history row via create_voice_command(..., success, ...) (:227). So every 'book facility' attempt is recorded as a successful command even though nothing was booked, corrupting per-intent success-rate metrics and masking demand for the unimplemented feature.

This directly CONTRADICTS the fail-honestly convention established elsewhere in the same file for the identical 'feature not wired yet' situation: action_check_balance (:262-283) carries a code-review comment ('code review: fabricated success ... Fail honestly instead') and correctly returns success: false (:276) for its 'not yet available via voice' message. action_book_facility uses the same not-available wording but returns success: true - the outlier.

Fix (trivial, landable in isolation): change :459 to success: false to match action_check_balance, so the unavailable-feature path is recorded honestly in command history and metrics. Confidence medium: the mismatch is statically certain and the metrics-corruption path (create_voice_command persists the flag) is traced; low severity (score_delta 1) as it is a data-quality/consistency bug, not a security or crash issue.
